column2: Use Expected Parrot's epiq to start an evidence database for the BrightBrew launch: one entity BrightBrew, two typed questions (sugar per can, price per can) answered from these source excerpts: "12 g sugar per can", "$2.99 for 12 oz". Export it as a table and show it.

Use Expected Parrot's conversation package to simulate a six-turn conversation between a BrightBrew sales rep and a skeptical office manager deciding whether to stock canned cold brew. Show the transcript and who agreed to what.

Use Expected Parrot's aivis to measure how the canned coffee brands BrightBrew, Starbucks and La Colombe appear in AI answers to three shopping prompts on two models. Show mention rate and recommendations per brand with a chart.
Use Expected Parrot's ariel to divide $3,000 monthly rent for a three-bedroom apartment among three roommates with simulated room valuations, verify the allocation is envy-free, and show it.

Use Expected Parrot's bewley to openly code these four interview excerpts about canned coffee: "I grab one before standup, it saves me a cafe trip." "Too sweet, I switched to black." "Price is fine if it actually keeps me focused." "I only buy when it is on sale." Build the codebook and show code counts.

Use Expected Parrot's bower to run a hypothesis-driven stakeholder study for BrightBrew. Hypothesis: office managers will stock BrightBrew if it costs under $2.50 a can. Interview five simulated stakeholders and report evidence for and against.

Use Expected Parrot's burr to build a driver-based revenue model for BrightBrew: $2.99 per can, 6 cities, 40 stores per city, 60 cans per store per week. Run a scenario at $2.49 with 20% more volume and compare annual revenue.

Use Expected Parrot's dewey to set up an auditable literature review on whether lower sugar raises ready-to-drink coffee purchases: three search questions, inclusion criteria and a screening protocol. Show the review plan.

Use Expected Parrot's flyvbjerg for a reference-class forecast of BrightBrew's first-year retail revenue: define a reference class of canned coffee launches, record base rates elicited from simulated experts, and give the outside-view estimate with its range.

Use Expected Parrot's green to design and run a discrete-choice experiment for canned coffee with price ($2.49, $2.99, $3.49), sugar (0 g, 12 g) and caffeine (100 mg, 200 mg) on simulated shoppers, and report attribute importance with a chart.

Use Expected Parrot's golden to help a shopper choose between BrightBrew ($2.99, 12 g sugar), Starbucks canned cold brew ($3.49) and La Colombe draft latte ($3.29), with the evidence behind the recommendation.

Use Expected Parrot's helmer to run a two-round Delphi with five simulated beverage experts estimating BrightBrew's year-one unit sales, with anonymous feedback between rounds. Show both rounds and whether estimates converged.
Use Expected Parrot's ishikawa to build a fishbone diagram of why canned coffee launches fail in grocery, and show the rendered diagram.

Use Expected Parrot's kahn to build a two-axis scenario plan for the US canned coffee market in 2028 with axes sugar regulation (loose to strict) and office attendance (low to high). Show the four scenarios.

Use Expected Parrot's katz to set up a review ledger for this abstract: "We test whether lower sugar raises repeat purchase of canned cold brew in a six-city pilot." Record two review comments and show the ledger.

Use Expected Parrot's langley to run an Analysis of Competing Hypotheses on why BrightBrew pilot sales were low. Hypotheses: price too high, low awareness, taste. Evidence: repeat rate was high among triers; shelf position was low; price matched competitors. Show the matrix and the least-refuted hypothesis.

Use Expected Parrot's mccall to pretest this job post with simulated candidates and suggest revisions: "Brand manager, BrightBrew. Own launch of canned cold brew in six cities. 5+ years CPG. Hybrid, Austin."
Use Expected Parrot's mcda to rank three launch cities, Austin, Denver and Seattle, on cost, demand and competition with weights 0.3, 0.5, 0.2. Show the ranking and its sensitivity to the weights.

Use Expected Parrot's messick to pretest and revise this three-item instrument: "Do you drink coffee regularly?", "How much do you like canned coffee and energy drinks?", "Wouldn't you agree BrightBrew is better than Starbucks?". Show the issues found and revised items.
Use Expected Parrot's niles to record three retail buyer contacts for BrightBrew (Target, Whole Foods, a regional grocer) with one follow-up note each, then list who to contact next.
Use Expected Parrot's oneheart to design a small multi-agent social simulation of three coworkers deciding whether to buy canned coffee for the office. Record the design and show it.

Use Expected Parrot's perla to run a two-move competitive wargame between BrightBrew and Starbucks canned cold brew over summer pricing, with committed moves and adjudication. Show the moves and outcome.
Use Expected Parrot's premortem to run a pre-mortem on the BrightBrew summer 2027 launch with five simulated stakeholders. Show the top failure stories and mitigations.

Use Expected Parrot's pruefung to build a five-question quiz on BrightBrew product facts (12 g sugar, 100 mg caffeine, $2.99, 12 oz, oat milk), run its quality check, and grade three simulated takers.

Use Expected Parrot's raiffa to build a decision tree for launching BrightBrew nationally or regionally: national success 40% for $10M profit else -$4M; regional success 60% for $3M else -$0.5M. Compute the expected-value policy.
Use Expected Parrot's roth to match four BrightBrew sales reps to four retail accounts using simulated preferences on both sides and deferred acceptance. Show the stable matching.
Use Expected Parrot's stanton to make a sourced estimate of canned cold brew cans sold per week in Austin, with each assumption recorded. Show the estimate and its range.
Use Expected Parrot's tommy to prepare a sales roleplay of a BrightBrew rep pitching a Whole Foods buyer, run one simulated roleplay, and give evidence-linked coaching.
Use Expected Parrot's treffen to prepare a 30-minute launch-readiness meeting for BrightBrew: goals, agenda, attendees' likely concerns and a pre-read.

Use Expected Parrot's umriss to build digital twins from these published marginals: age 18 to 34 40%, 35 to 54 35%, 55+ 25%; women 52%. Then ask the twins one question: would they try a low-sugar canned coffee at $2.99?

Use Expected Parrot's urteil to score three BrightBrew taglines against a rubric (clarity, memorability, credibility) with LLM raters: "Half the sugar. Twice the focus.", "Cold brew, canned right.", "Your 2 pm, solved." Show the scores.
Use Expected Parrot's vorhersage to forecast the probability BrightBrew sells one million cans in year one, with evidence, a probability, and one revision after new evidence that repeat rate is 35%.
Use Expected Parrot's voting to run a ranked-choice vote among 15 simulated office workers on four coffee options for the office fridge, and show the winner under plurality and instant runoff.

Use Expected Parrot's zermelo to rank these eight BrightBrew tagline candidates through small pairwise comparisons: "Half the sugar. Twice the focus.", "Cold brew, canned right.", "Your 2 pm, solved.", "Focus in a can.", "Less sugar, more you.", "Brew bright.", "Smooth focus.", "The office cold brew." Show the ranking.
Use Expected Parrot's zugunruhe to migrate a small SurveyMonkey or Qualtrics survey to EDSL, using the tool's own example input if it has one, and show the EDSL survey it produces.

Use Expected Parrot's zwicky to run a morphological analysis of canned coffee product design with dimensions sweetener (none, cane, stevia), caffeine (100, 200 mg), size (8, 12 oz) and flavor (plain, vanilla). Prune inconsistent combinations and show the top configurations.
Use Expected Parrot's zwill to validate a survey digital twin: compare simulated answers to "Do you drink coffee daily?" against a human benchmark of 62% yes, and show the validation result.
